items.job: Replace rusted brake lines (full preformed line set)
items.note: Price is for replacing all the steel lines. Fixing one short section costs much less. Rusted fittings can add time.

items.t: Clunk felt in the steering wheel
items.job: Replace intermediate steering shaft
items.note: Some shops first try lubricating the shaft per GM bulletin, which costs less but the clunk may come back.

items.job: Replace transfer case shift encoder motor
items.note: Includes basic diagnosis. A bad front axle actuator, switch or control module are other common causes.

items.t: Instrument cluster gauges stick or quit
items.job: Rebuild instrument cluster (replace gauge stepper motors)
items.note: Mail-in rebuild services are the cheapest route. Old GM special coverage for some trucks has likely expired; ask a dealer.

items.job: Replace pistons and rings (GM oil consumption fix)
items.note: Shops often try a valve cover/PCV fix or AFM disable first, which costs far less. Engine replacement costs much more.

items.job: Replace valve lifters and camshaft
items.note: If caught early, replacing only the lifters on one bank costs less. Metal in the oil can mean more engine work.

items.job: Replace upper dash pad
items.note: A molded dash cover that fits over the cracks is a much cheaper fix.

items.t: Hard brake pedal from vacuum pump failure (recall)
items.job: Replace brake vacuum pump
items.note: Often free under GM's recall. Check your VIN first or ask a Chevrolet dealer.

items.job: Replace A/C condenser and recharge system
items.note: Price includes leak testing. If the compressor also failed, expect much more.

items.t: Lifter failure on V8s with cylinder deactivation
items.job: Replace valve lifters and camshaft
items.note: Newer trucks may still be under powertrain warranty. Engine damage from metal debris raises the cost a lot.

items.job: Transmission fluid exchange with updated GM fluid
items.note: May be covered by powertrain warranty. If the torque converter must be replaced, expect much more.

items.job: Replace rear driveshaft
items.note: Free under GM's recall for affected trucks. Check your VIN first or ask a Chevrolet dealer.

items.job: Reprogram transmission control software (recall remedy)
items.note: Free under GM recall. Check your VIN first. Some trucks also get a new valve body, which costs far more if not covered.

items.job: Replace engine assembly
items.note: Covered by GM's L87 recall for affected trucks. Check your VIN or ask the dealer before paying for anything.

items.job: Replace engine coolant flow control valve
items.note: GM special coverage may pay for this. Check your VIN or ask a Chevrolet dealer first.

items.t: Transfer case can lock the wheels - do not drive (recall)
items.job: Inspect and replace the transfer case
items.note: Do not drive. Free under recall 26V-289. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Rear bumper bracket may be too weak to tow (recall)
items.job: Replace rear bumper bracket and trailer hitch
items.note: Free under recall 24V-626. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Brake warning light may not come on when fluid is low (recall)
items.job: Update brake control module software
items.note: Free under recall 24V-674. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Daytime running lights stay on with the headlights (recall)
items.job: Update body control module software
items.note: Free under recall 22V-903. Check the VIN first.

items.t: 6.2L V8 engine failures outside the recall window (federal investigation)
items.job: Replace the engine long block after rod bearing failure
items.note: Free only if the VIN falls under recall 25V-274; engines built after that window are covered by investigation EA26005, not a repair order.
